en.headline: Transport bureau to review bus fare applications of up to 17.7 per cent carefully
en.dek: Citybus seeks the largest rise while KMB asks for 16 per cent; lawmakers at Friday's panel meeting criticised the scale and raised service issues.
body: Four franchised bus operators have applied for fare increases ranging from 8.1 per cent to 17.7 per cent, citing sharp rises in fuel costs linked to developments in the Middle East and other operating pressures.

Citybus has applied for 17.7 per cent, Kowloon Motor Bus for 16 per cent, New Lantao Bus for 9.8 per cent and Long Win Bus for 8.1 per cent. Representatives told the Legislative Council's transport panel on Friday that fuel prices had created a significant financial burden and that passenger numbers remained below pre-pandemic levels.

The Transport and Logistics Bureau said it would handle the applications prudently, taking into account public acceptability, operators' financial sustainability, service quality and other factors. A final proposal would be submitted to the Chief Executive and the Executive Council after consulting the Transport Advisory Board. Several lawmakers said the proposed increases exceeded inflation and expressed concern about affordability and service reliability.

zh.headline: 運物局稱審慎處理巴士加價申請 加幅介乎8.1%至17.7%
zh.dek: 城巴申請加價17.7%為最高，九巴申請16%，立法會交通事務委員會周五討論時議員批評加幅過高。
body: 四間專營巴士營辦商向政府提交加價申請，幅度由8.1%至17.7%不等，主要理由包括中東局勢導致燃油成本急升及其他營運壓力。
城巴申請加價17.7%，九巴申請16%，嶼巴申請9.8%，龍運申請8.1%。營辦商代表周五在立法會交通事務委員會上表示，燃油價格上升造成重大財政負擔，而乘客人次仍未回復至疫情前水平。
運輸及物流局表示會以審慎嚴謹態度處理申請，整全考慮公眾接受程度、營辦商財務可持續性、服務質素等因素。在諮詢交通諮詢委員會後，最終建議將提交行政長官及行政會議考慮。多名議員批評加幅超出通脹，關注基層負擔能力及服務可靠性。
